# Surgery Advanced procedures let medical staff **open a patient layer-by-layer**, repair or replace anatomy, and close everything back up. Surgery is precise work: use the right tools, prefer a **sterile operating surface**, and watch your patient's stability while you operate.
This page covers gear, environment, and how to think through a procedure. For synthetic replacements after removal, see [textlink="Cybernetics" link="Cybernetics"].
## Before you cut - **Assess the patient** with a health analyzer or medical PDA ([textlink="Medical Doctor" link="MedicalDoctor"]) so you know damage types, bleeding, and overall stability. - **Secure your workspace**: buckling a conscious patient to a table or bed reduces movement. A patient moving can interrupt surgery. - **Prepare the OR**: sterile masks, clean floors, surgical flooring, non-rusted-walls, and many other factors can make for an unclean operating room.
## Sterile surfaces & positioning The gold standard is an **operating table** built for surgery.
Regular medical beds are excellent for stabilizing a patient, but are not as sterile. They make for a good alternative when an operating table is not available.
## The surgical toolkit Each step expects a **specific tool quality**. Dedicated surgical instruments perform reliably; improvised substitutes often **take longer** and injure the patient.
### Carrying it all Medical belts commonly whitelist surgical gear so you can **stay organized** during long procedures.
If you misplace your tools, cargo can provide a surgical crate to replace them. If your cargo department is extremely well funded, you may even be able to afford a Cyber Surgery Crate.
## How procedures flow Each step will inform you of the proper tool, and the improvised tool. Such as (Scalpel/Cutting). Which indicates the proper tool is a scalpel, but that you can improvise any cutting tool for the step.
## Organs, limbs, and grafts Removing damaged anatomy is only half the battle—you still need a viable replacement **before** you leave cavities exposed:
- **Natural organs** harvested safely must be stored until reimplantation (remember metabolism stops helping once critical organs are gone). - **Cybernetic organs and limbs** must be fabricated or sourced ahead of time; installation still routes through surgery ([textlink="Cybernetics" link="Cybernetics"]).
Most animal organs support xenograft of organs. These organs are most often far worse than any species employed by NT, but exceptions may exist.
